definitions.explanation: The overall standard of well-being, comfort, and satisfaction in a person's daily life. Commonly used in medical, social welfare, and policy contexts.

examples.japanese: {生活|せいかつ}の{質|しつ}を{向上|こうじょう}させたい。
examples.english: I want to improve my quality of life.

examples.japanese: この{治療|ちりょう}は{患者|かんじゃ}の{生活|せいかつ}の{質|しつ}を{大|おお}きく{改善|かいぜん}する。
examples.english: This treatment greatly improves the patient's quality of life.

examples.japanese: {高齢者|こうれいしゃ}の{生活|せいかつ}の{質|しつ}を{維持|いじ}するためには、{地域|ちいき}の{支援|しえん}が{欠|か}かせない。
examples.english: Community support is essential for maintaining the quality of life of the elderly.

notes:
USAGE:
Often abbreviated as QOL (キューオーエル) in medical and welfare contexts. Frequently discussed in relation to healthcare, aging, disability support, and urban planning. The English abbreviation QOL is widely understood in Japanese professional settings.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {生活|せいかつ}の{質|しつ}を{高|たか}める (to enhance quality of life)
- {生活|せいかつ}の{質|しつ}の{向上|こうじょう} (improvement in quality of life)
- {生活|せいかつ}の{質|しつ}を{維持|いじ}する (to maintain quality of life)
- {生活|せいかつ}の{質|しつ}が{低下|ていか}する (quality of life declines)
